title: Five chambers in the rack: where do the tabs go?
question: You asked for numbered tabs on the bar. The bar turns out to have 0-1 pixels spare at its tightest spacing, so a tab has to be a strip beside the bar rather than a cell in it -- which edge should it eat? A covers the soil, B covers the ceiling and paints over the top HUD line, C spends nothing and only tells you which chamber you are in when you open the menu.
context_md:
Same rack, same warm-up, three placements. **The frame counts under each are the point**: chamber 1 has run 864 ticks and chambers 2-5 are held at 0, so the freeze is real rather than a picture of five copies of one box.

A switch is a swap, not a rebuild -- a parked chamber resumes on the tick it stopped at.

- **A** strip along the top of the bar. Reads as part of the bar. Eats the bed's stone floor, which `scene.rs` already sits flush with the bar, so it is the edge with least in it.
- **B** strip at the top of the screen. Same pixels, but it covers the ceiling shell and the lamps -- and, visible in the shot, **paints over the first line of the PAUSED readout**.
- **C** no tabs at all. `SHIFT+1..5` switches, `F4` opens the full rack. Costs nothing and shows nothing.

Either strip is drawn **only when the rack holds more than one chamber**, so the lab's own opening -- one empty box -- pays nothing in all three.
